title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Taiwan Semiconductor, Intel, Apple, Alphabet, NVIDIA, iShares Semiconductor ETF, Advanced Micro Devices and Arm
content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – August 23, 2024 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. TSM, Intel Corp. INTC, Apple Inc. AAPL, Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, NVIDIA Corporation NVDA, iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD and Arm Holdings plc ARM.

Here are highlights from Thursday’s Analyst Blog:

The Better Semiconductor Stock to Buy Now: TSM or INTC

The semiconductor industry has witnessed stupendous growth over the past four decades, with chips becoming an integral part of electronic devices like computers and smartphones, to name a few. An increase in acceptance of emerging technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to fuel demand for semiconductors.

Manufacturing, healthcare, and retail sectors have already integrated digital technologies that require robust semiconductor solutions. Thus, the global semiconductor industry is likely to witness a CAGR of 14.9% from 2024 to 2032, hitting $2062.59 billion by 2032, per Fortune Business Insights.

However, despite the positive trend, picking the top semiconductor stocks is challenging since their sales fluctuate incessantly. So, here is one chip stock to buy right away — Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. — and one industry bigwig to shun — Intel Corp.

2 Reasons to Be Bullish on TSM

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing expects healthy demand for its chips as more companies begin to implement AI features in smartphones. Apple Inc.’s initiative to launch the iPhone 16 this fall should boost demand for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s chips. The new “Apple Intelligence” system has already benefited Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. Apple is one of the biggest clients of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and accounts for around one-fourth of TSM’s revenues.

Demand for AI applications like Alphabet Inc.’s Gemini and Open AI’s ChatGPT has increased noticeably. But such applications require huge data, kept in data centers, which rely on graphic processing units (GPUs) that NVIDIA Corporation manufactures. And without TSM’s manufacturing prowess, the GPUs can’t be operative. So, in a way, the surging demand for AI applications would continue to boost Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s sales over the next several years and help its shares soar.

No doubt, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s earnings outlook for the current year remains promising, with the $6.45 Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings per share up 11.4% from a year ago.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s shares have already outperformed the iShares Semiconductor ETF this year (+64.6% vs. +22.6%).

2 Reasons to be Bearish on INTC

Intel, regrettably, is losing its competitive edge over its rival Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Intel is in a fix after failing to make much progress in its foundry business. AMD has progressed significantly in producing high-performance processing machinery. Intel’s failure to take advantage of the ever-growing AI applications industry is alarming against the strong growth posted by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, which is currently the industry standard.

On the other hand, Arm Holdings plc is disrupting Intel’s server, storage, and networking space. ARM’s designs in the micro server segment have witnessed espousal by quite a lot of Intel’s competitors. As a result, Intel’s earnings outlook for the current year remains bleak, with the $0.38 Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings per share down a massive 77.5% from a year ago.

Intel’s shares have underperformed SOXX year to date, down 57.4%. Notably, both Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Intel are listed in SOXX.

TSM Fundamentals – Very Strong

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, by the way, has generated profits more competently than Intel. This is because TSM has a return on equity (ROE) of 25.5%, while Intel’s is around 4.4%. As a thumb rule, any reading above 20% is primarily considered very strong.

Meanwhile, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing is a solid dividend payer, which is indicative of a stable business model. Its dividend payout ratio sits at 31% of earnings, a low payout that indicates the company is reinvesting the bulk of its earnings in research and development, a must for growth. Whereas, Intel’s dividend payout ratio is 109% of earnings, which is unsustainable.

TSM Less Pricey Than INTC

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s shares are less expensive than Intel’s, which has given the integrated circuit foundry an edge over the world’s largest semiconductor company. After all, buying INTC’s shares will burn a larger hole in your wallet than the TSM stock.

This is because, per the Price/Earnings ratio, TSM stock presently trades at 26.5X forward earnings. However, INTC’s forward earnings multiple is 56.6X.

TSM to Buy Hand Over Fist

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, rightfully, is a better buy than Intel as it is well-positioned to make the most of the growth in AI, can generate profit consistently, and has a lower valuation.

Prominent brokers have also increased the average short-term price target of TSM by almost 19% from the company’s last closing price of $172.04. The analysts’ highest price target is at $250.

title: The Cheapest Trillion-Dollar Stock: Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, or Meta?
content:
Six U.S. companies are valued at $1 trillion or more, and they all operate in the technology sector:

Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL): $3.44 trillion Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT): $3.16 trillion Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA): $3.14 trillion Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL)(NASDAQ: GOOG): $2.07 trillion Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN): $1.87 trillion Meta Platforms(NASDAQ: META): $1.33 trillion

All of these companies are profitable, so they can be valued with the widely used price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio. It's calculated by dividing the share price of a given company by its earnings per share. The Nasdaq-100 index trades at a P/E ratio of 30.9, which is a good reference point: NVDA PE Ratio Chart

Nvidia is the most expensive trillion-dollar stock today on a P/E basis. However, the company is growing so quickly it has a forward P/E ratio of just 33.1 based on next year's earnings forecast. In other words, its valuation is much more reasonable if investors are willing to hold it for a couple of years.

The cheapest stock of the group is Alphabet. A judge recently ruled that Google Search is a monopoly, and the U.S. Department of Justice wants to break up the company to resolve that issue. It could take years -- if it happens at all -- but combined with growing competition from artificial intelligence chatbots, which are threatening the dominance of Google Search, investors are treading cautiously with respect to Alphabet's valuation.

Finally, Amazon deserves a mention. It's on track to generate $635 billion in revenue this year, which is more than any of its peers, and it trades at the cheapest price-to-sales ratio (which divides a company's market capitalization by its revenue). Plus, its earnings are forecast to grow 63% this year and 23% in 2025, so its elevated P/E ratio might actually be justified.

In summary, a P/E ratio alone isn't always the best indicator of value. Investors could easily make the case that despite trading at triple the P/E ratio, Nvidia stock is a better buy than Alphabet because of its rapid growth (and Alphabet's regulatory headwinds).

title: Germany in ‘real mess’ as manufacturing crisis spills over
content:
German Chancellor Olaf Scholz at the Paris Olympics last month - SARAH MEYSSONNIER

Germany’s economic woes have deepened after new figures showed a second straight month of contraction.

S&P Global’s composite PMI showed a reading of 48.5 for Germany in August, down from 49.1 the previous month and below economists’ forecasts.

The downturn was driven by an ongoing crisis in Germany’s dominant manufacturing sector, which has now been in contraction for more than two years.

But these troubles have now started to spill over into the services sector, which had otherwise been steady.

In a further blow, employment in Europe’s largest economy decreased at the fastest rate in four years as firms expressed less optimism towards growth prospects in the coming year.

Dr Cyrus de la Rubia, chief economist at Hamburg Commercial Bank, branded the numbers a “real mess”.

He said: “The recession in Germany’s manufacturing sector deepened in August, with no recovery in sight. In fact, new orders took a sharper dive than last month, mainly due to a significant drop in foreign demand, signalling more trouble ahead.

“Given this, it’s hardly surprising that companies are ramping up staff cuts and slashing inventories of inputs even more aggressively than before.”

Read the latest updates below.

06:01 PM BST

Signing off...

Thanks for joining us today. The Markets blog will be back in the morning, but I’ll leave you with of the top business stories elsewhere on The Telegraph website today:

Elon Musk cuts down 500,000 trees at Tesla’s German gigafactory Capital gains raid by Reeves risks costing taxpayer £2bn Ben Marlow: Jet-setting Starbucks boss makes a mockery of the company’s green agenda

05:54 PM BST

European stocks rise on rate cut hopes

Europe’s main stock index climbed on Thursday, with healthcare and retail stocks leading the charge, while investors cheered the prospects of interest rate cuts by central banks, despite some nervousness by traders in the US, and sifted through a wave of economic data globally.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 index closed 0.4pc higher, rising for the second day and closing at its highest level this month.

The retail sector was the strongest part of the market, boosted by an 10.7pc jump in JD Sports, after the British sportswear retailer reported an improvement in second-quarter underlying sales growth.

The healthcare sector hit a record high, in part due to a 2.4pc rise in drug company Novo Nordisk.

05:46 PM BST

Apple bows to EU regulators over browser choices

Apple will change how iPhone and iPad users in the EU choose their web browser, the company said today.

The iPhone maker came under pressure from regulators to make changes after the EU’s sweeping Digital Markets Act took effect on March 7, forcing it to offer mobile users the ability to select from a list of available web browsers on a “choice screen” the first time they open Safari.

Story continues

In an update later this year, Apple users will be able to select a default browser directly from the choice screen after going through a mandatory list of options.

A randomly ordered list of 12 browsers per EU country will be shown to the user with short descriptions, and the chosen one will be automatically downloaded, Apple said.

It will also add a dedicated section for changing default apps and make more apps deletable.

Apple released a previous update in response to the new rules in March, but browser companies criticised the design of its choice screen, and the Commission opened an investigation on March 25 saying it suspected that the measures fell short of effective compliance.

Apple said it has been in dialogue with the European Commission and believes the new changes will address regulators’ concerns. Apple chief Tim Cook holds up an iPhone 15 Pro last September at an event in Cupertino, California - Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

05:43 PM BST

Trump promotes family-run crypto platform

Donald Trump has promoted the upcoming launch of a cryptocurrency platform, presenting it as an alternative to banks and financial institutions.

He wrote on his Truth Social network:

For too long, the average American has been squeezed by the big banks and financial elites.

It’s time we take a stand - together.

Mr Trump provided no details as to the exact content of the project, called “The DeFiant Ones”.

His post featured the now iconic picture of the former president, fist clenched, just moments after an assassination attempt last month at a rally in Pennsylvania.

Two of his sons, Eric and Donald Jr, who head the Trump Organisation family conglomerate, have described the project in recent weeks as “digital real estate”.

During his presidency Trump referred to cryptocurrencies as a scam, but has since radically changed his position, presenting himself as a “pro-bitcoin president” if elected in November.

In so doing, he is standing in opposition to the Biden administration, which is seen as a proponent of regulating the sector.

05:37 PM BST

Nestle replaces chief executive with company veteran

Nestle is replacing Chief Executive Mark Schneider with long-serving executive Laurent Freixe, the company said today, a big change at the world’s biggest foodmaker which has struggled with the cost of living crisis hitting customers.

Mr Schneider has decided to relinquish his roles as chief executive and member of the board after eight years leading the company, Nestle said.

Nestle has struggled recently, last month cutting its full-year sales outlook, saying it had had to slow its price hikes as cash-strapped customers become more price conscious.

Shares at the maker of KitKat chocolate bars and Nestle instant coffee have fallen 8pc in 2024, underperforming rivals such as Unilever which have gained 29pc.

Mr Freixe joined Nestle in 1986, and has been on the Swiss company’s executive board for 16 years.

The switch to Mr Freixe is a return to the Nestle’s normal practice of promoting chief executives from within the company.

Mr Schneider, the former boss of German healthcare company Fresenius, was Nestle’s first external hire for its top job in nearly a century when he took charge in 2016. Laurent Freixe takes up the role on September 1 - Edgard Garrido/Reuters

05:21 PM BST

‘Markets are preparing for possible turbulence on Friday’, says analyst

Markets are “preparing for possible turbulence” tomorrow, an analyst has said, amid uncertain trading in stocks today.

Stock markets wobbled this afternoon as investors await a highly-anticipated speech by US Federal Reserve chief Jerome Powell, hoping he will drop more clues about an expected interest-rate cut.

The Dow, the broader S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq had all opened on the right foot, extending gains from the previous day, but faltered later this afternoon.

In Europe, Paris finished flat while London and Frankfurt were in the green but not as strong as earlier in the day when key surveys showed business activity accelerated in Britain and the eurozone in August.

The spotlight will turn to Powell on Friday when he addresses an annual gathering of global central bankers in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, with investors eager to hear for fresh signals about the Fed’s plans.

Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank, said:

We can see the mounting tension [heading] into Powell’s speech.

Markets are preparing for possible turbulence on Friday.

05:13 PM BST

Junior lawyers offered £38,000 referral bonuses in war for talent

Junior lawyers are being offered bonuses of $50,000 (£38,000) for referring their friends for jobs amid a war for talent. Adam Mawardi reports:

US law firms Paul Weiss and Kirkland & Ellis are paying tens of thousands of pounds to London-based workers as part of the firm’s global policies.

The bonuses are on top of six-figure salaries paid to junior lawyers, which start at £180,000 at Paul Weiss and £164,000 at Kirkland & Ellis upon qualification.

Kirkland & Ellis has extended its $50,000 referral bonus scheme until January 2025, according to the Financial Times.

The Chicago-based firm previously offered incentives of $25,000, but doubled this last October.

London’s homegrown law firms are facing renewed pressure from foreign rivals amid a rebound in demand for legal services from last year’s deal-making slump.

Read the full story...

04:55 PM BST

FTSE 100 closes marginally up after afternoon of subdued trading

The FTSE 100 closed up 0.1pc, having given up some of the gains it made this morning.

JD Sports was the biggest riser, up 10.7pc, followed by Tesco, up 2pc.

At the other end of the index, Legal & General fell 2.8pc, followed by natural resources company Glencore, down 1.9pc.

Meanwhile, the mid-cap FTSE 250 fell 0.4pc. North Atlantic Smaller Companies rose 2.9pc, followed by recruiter Hays, up 2.5pc.

Diversified Energy was the biggest faller, down 5.8pc, followed by Ithaca Energy, down 5.5pc.

04:51 PM BST

BMW beats Tesla to lead Europe’s electric-vehicle market for the first time

BMW rose above Tesla to be the best selling electric vehicle seller for the first time last month.

Bloomberg reported that sales of fully electric BMWs in Europe jumped by more than a third to 14,869 units in July, according to data from Jato Dynamics. Tesla’s registrations fell 16pc to 14,561 units. A BMW i3 electric Metropolitan Police car outside the Houses of Parliament, 2019 - John Keeble/Getty Images

04:48 PM BST

US home sales ended a 4-month slide in July amid easing mortgage rates

Sales of previously occupied American homes ended a four-month slide in July as easing mortgage rates and a pickup in properties on the market encouraged buyers.

Existing home sales rose 1.3pc last month from June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.95m, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) said this afternoon.

Sales fell 2.5pc compared with July last year and are running below last year’s pace. The latest home sales came in slightly higher than the 3.92m pace economists were expecting.

Lawrence Yun, the NAR’s chief economist, said:

Despite the modest gain, home sales are still sluggish. But consumers are definitely seeing more choices, and affordability is improving due to lower interest rates.

04:43 PM BST

Wall Street falls as traders bet on slower US rate cuts

Wall Street shares have fallen during trade this afternoon amid pessimism in the markets of the pace of US interest rate cuts.

Since yesterday, traders have cut their bets on a more than quarter point interest rate cut in September, amid expectations among some commentators that Jerome Powell, the Fed chair, will pour cold water over large and fast rate cuts between now and the end of the year.

It came as Patrick Harker, the Philadelphia Fed president, told Reuters: “I think a slow, methodical approach down is the right way to go.”

Share prices in Europe and the US have been mostly been subdued this afternoon, but the S&P is down 0.4pc, the Dow Jones is down 0.3pc and the Nasdaq Composite is down 0.8pc.

04:27 PM BST

BP shares drop to lowest for two years

Shares in BP fell as much as 1.4pc today, reaching their lowest in two years.

Henry Tarr, an analyst at Berenberg, said:

BP pivoted hard toward the energy transition under Bernard Looney around the time of maximum interest in green energy solutions and very low interest rates.

Since then commodity prices have recovered, making the legacy upstream business seem more attractive, while higher interest rates and more competition has left some low-carbon businesses looking less attractive.

Will Hares, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said:

Compared to its No. 1 peer, Shell, there’s an increasing concern of sustainability of returns. The market wants to see more of a commitment to essentially their cash engines, which are oil and gas.

In June, The Telegraph reported that BP has put all new offshore wind projects on pause as its new chief executive, Murray Auchincloss, sought to focus more heavily on fossil fuels.

04:25 PM BST

Euro zone bond yields edge up after strong survey data

Euro zone bond yields were rose today after survey data showed the bloc’s services sector fared better than expected in August.

Germany’s 10-year bond yield, the benchmark for the euro zone, was at 2.245pc, up from 2.194pc yesterday.

Purchasing managers’ index (PMI) survey data showed euro zone business activity was surprisingly strong in August, with services a bright spot.

Germany remained mired in a downturn, however. Its PMI showed business activity contracted in August for a second consecutive month and by more than expected.

Separate figures showed growth in negotiated wages in the euro zone slowed sharply to 3.55pc year-on-year in the second quarter, down from a record high of 4.74pc in the first quarter.

Jussi Hiljanen, head of European rates strategy at financial services group SEB, said:

The PMI figures are overshadowing these wage numbers. The service sector is still strong and service sector inflation is one of the focal points of the ECB [European Central Bank].

04:08 PM BST

UK and US stock markets flat despite Japanese jump

Major stock market indexes in the UK and America are mostly not far from being flat currently, with earlier gains tailing off. However, on the continent, the Dax is up 0.3pc and the pan-European Stoxx 600 is up 0.4pc.

Axel Rudolph, senior technical analyst at online trading platform IG, said:

The .... rally in the Japanese Nikkei 225 hasn’t been replicated by any US, nor European equity indices, which continue to trade in low volume and volatility ahead of Fed chair Powell’s speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday.

03:51 PM BST

Traders are pricing in too many US rate cuts, says former Pimco boss

Traders are “overdoing” their bets on US interest rate cuts, the former boss of investment management firm Pimco has said.

Mohamed El-Erian, the president of Queens’ College, Cambridge, told Bloomberg Television:

It is problematic in my mind that the market is pricing in so many rate cuts right now. The market is overdoing it.

03:46 PM BST

JD Sports shares surge 8.2pc as Americans drive sales

JD Sports shares are the strongest performers among the FTSE 100 today, rising 8.2pc after reporting growing sales.

The high street retailer said its total sales grew 2.4pc over the three months to August, compared with the same period a year ago, and on a like-for-like basis, which strips out the impact of new store openings.

This was driven by growth in North America and Europe, whereas sales in the UK slipped 0.8pc year on year, the group said.

It flagged a decline in earnings generated from clothing and online sales, which particularly dragged on the UK.

Chief executive Regis Schultz stressed that there continues to be demand for new trainers among its younger demographic of shoppers. He said:

The trend around sneakers and more relaxed apparel continues.

There is a little bit of movement around brands, with some seeing some innovation, but I think we see strong appetite from the consumer and especially the young customer ... and that is what we are benefiting from.

Nike is still “by far the number one” brand, while there is “still some room to go for Adidas to catch up”, Mr Schultz said.

Richard Hunter, head of markets at Interactive Investor, said:

Perhaps the most exciting and obvious opportunity in the medium term is JD’s growing brand presence in the major US market. There is 'still some room to go for Adidas to catch up', said JD Sports boss Regis Schultz - Lisi Niesner/Reuters

03:32 PM BST

Stock markets buoyed by US rate cut hopes

Stock markets are mostly up today on growing optimism that the US Federal Reserve will cut interest rates next month.

Wall Street got off on the right foot at the open, adding to the previous day’s gains, although they are currently roughly flat compared with the open.

London, Paris and Frankfurt are up in afternoon deals after Tokyo and Hong Kong finished higher.

The dollar has been under pressure from expectations of lower rates, though it pared down some losses against the euro and the yen today.

Investor confidence in a rate cut grew after minutes from the Fed’s July policy meeting, released last night, showed that most members believed that it would be “appropriate” to lower borrowing costs in September.

Traders were also buoyed by official figures showing that US employers added around 68,000 fewer jobs monthly in the year to March than initially estimated.

A softer US labour market, along with cooling inflation, gives the central bank room to start reducing rates that were brought to a 23-year high in order to bring down soaring consumer prices.

The markets are now eagerly anticipating a speech by Fed chief Jerome Powell at an annual gathering of global central bankers in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday for more signs that a cut is imminent. The New York Stock Exchange pictured yesterday - Peter Morgan/AP Photo

03:02 PM BST

British defence contractor to work on top secret nuclear monitoring base Pituffik was established during the Cold War to detect intercontinental ballistic missiles flying over the North Pole - RITZAU SCANPIX

Defence services firm Serco has landed a $320m (£250m) contract to build an emergency power station at a top secret nuclear monitoring base in Thule, Greenland’s northernmost town.

Christopher Jasper has more:

The deal will see Serco boost the capacity of a backup power plant at a US space base, where an array of sensors are in place to detect nuclear attacks from intercontinental ballistic missiles fired over the North Pole.

The four-year contract, awarded by the US Army Corps of Engineers, starts this month and will see Serco provide what boss Mark Irwin said will be a “mission-critical upgrade” in a “pivotal location”.

The Pituffik space base, established during the Cold War, also performs surveillance by tracking satellites and spacecraft as they orbit the planet.

Thule, named after the Latin word for the world’s most far-flung location, has a population of about 650 people, who are mostly military personnel from the US and Denmark.

Read Christopher’s full story here

02:50 PM BST

Wall Street opens higher on rising rate cut hopes

US stocks have started the day on the front foot as investor hopes pick up that the Federal Reserve will start cutting interest rates next month.

The benchmark S&P 500 rose 0.3pc and the Dow Jones was up 0.1pc, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained 0.4pc.

02:28 PM BST

Jack Daniel’s owner to scrap diversity goals Jack Daniel's whisky

The owner of Jack Daniel’s whisky has become the latest company to scrap its diversity goals following a backlash from conservatives.

Brown-Forman, which is the largest wine and spirits company in the US, has told staff it will stop linking executive pay to progress on diversity, equality and inclusion.

It will also stop taking part in an annual ranking of companies with a LGBTQ-friendly work environment and scrap plans to try and work with more suppliers from a minority background.

In the email, Brown-Forman said: “The world has evolved, our business has changed, and the legal and external landscape has shifted dramatically, particularly within the United States.

“With these new dynamics at play, we must adjust our work to ensure it continues to drive business results while appropriately recognising the current environment in which we find ourselves.”

It comes amid growing pressure on companies to abandon policies considered “woke” by campaigners such as anti-DEI activist Robby Starbuck.

Harley-Davidson also dropped its diversity targets earlier this week following pressure from Starbuck.

01:46 PM BST

US jobless claims rise ahead of Fed decision

The number of Americans filing for unemployment benefits rose in the latest week, though the overall cooling of the US labour market appears to still be on track.

Initial claims for state unemployment benefits rose 4,000 to a seasonally adjusted 232,000 for the week ending August 17, according to Labor Department figures. That compares to economists’ forecasts of 230,000 claims.

However, the figures should help to ease concerns of a downturn in the US job market after a surprise slump in job gains last month.

The Federal Reserve will have a keen eye on the figures as they consider whether to start cutting interest rates in September.

01:28 PM BST

Travelodge suffers ‘softer’ demand despite Taylor Swift boost

Travelodge has reported “softer” demand for its hotel rooms in London despite a boost from Taylor Swift’s Eras tour.

The budget hotel chain said it enjoyed strong trading close to the popstar’s Wembley concerts and around major sporting events.

But there was lower demand during Wimbledon and fewer midweek leisure visitors to the capital due to poor weather.

The downturn was offset by strong regional demand for hotel rooms, with bosses hailing “encouraging trends” for staycations in the UK in June.

Overall, revenue was up 1.7pc to £486.7m for the first six months of 2024, compared with the same period a year earlier.

Jo Boydell, chief executive of Travelodge, said:

The UK regions have been really solid this year but London has been impacted by a lower event schedule year-on-year.

For the bigger events we have had, such as Taylor Swift and big sporting events, we have performed really well. The return of the football season has been really good as well, with that supporting a lot of regional hotels.

12:52 PM BST

Peloton grows revenue as turnaround starts to pay off Peloton

Peloton has posted better-than-expected revenue and profits in its latest quarter in a sign the struggling fitness firm’s turnaround plan is starting to bear fruit.

The New York-based company, which makes interactive exercise equipment, posted sales of $644m (£491m) in the three months to the end of June.

That was up less than 1pc from a year earlier, but was comfortably ahead of Wall Street’s forecasts.

Peloton also said it was “especially proud” of its move towards profitability. Adjusted earnings were $70.3m, compared to a loss of $34.7m a year earlier.

In a letter to shareholders, the company said: “We’ll continue to optimise our expenses. Our improvement in profitability reflects our continued focus on aligning our costs with the size of our business.”

12:32 PM BST

How airports became a battleground for a looming Labour revolt Heathrow Airport - Jack Taylor/Getty Images

Heathrow and Gatwick expansion plans risk a Labour backbench rebellion, reports our transport industry editor Christopher Jasper:

When Labour announced this week that it would back the expansion of London City airport against the wishes of local party members, the decision reverberated far beyond east London.

By riding roughshod over Newham council’s bid to block thousands of additional flights, Labour put down a marker in the first significant test of its stance on controversial infrastructure projects likely to boost GDP but have a negative impact on the environment.

The decision to lift London City’s annual capacity by 2.5m passengers, or almost 40pc, gave substance to Labour’s pledge to make economic growth its key policy driver.

In doing so, it also bolstered the view that the party leadership may be willing to lock horns with its own MPs when it comes to one of Britain’s fiercest infrastructure debates – that is the construction of new runways at Heathrow and Gatwick.

Read his full story here.

11:48 AM BST

Elon Musk cuts down 500,000 trees at Tesla’s German gigafactory

Elon Musk’s Tesla felled half a million trees in order to build his giant Berlin electric car factory, satellite analysis shows.

Here’s Matt Field with more:

Imaging from environmental intelligence firm Kayrros suggested around 329 hectares of local woodland were felled between March 2020 and May 2023 to expand the plant. This is equivalent to around 500,000 trees.

Work on the plant, which has capacity to produce 500,000 electric vehicles each year, began in 2020 and it officially opened in 2022. It is Tesla’s only so-called “gigafactory” in Europe.

The extent to which Tesla has altered the local environment, according to satellite images shared with the Guardian, is likely to reignite controversy surrounding the factory.

Read the full story here

11:25 AM BST

Reaction: German numbers are a ‘real mess’

Dr Cyrus de la Rubia, chief economist at Hamburg Commercial Bank, offers a damning assessment of Germany’s PMI numbers:

These numbers are a real mess. The recession in Germany’s manufacturing sector deepened in August, with no recovery in sight. In fact, new orders took a sharper dive than last month, mainly due to a significant drop in foreign demand, signalling more trouble ahead. Given this, it’s hardly surprising that companies are ramping up staff cuts and slashing inventories of inputs even more aggressively than before.

The struggles in manufacturing are starting to spill over into the otherwise steady services sector. For the third month in a row, services activity growth has slowed down. New business is barely growing, and backlogs declined once again. The export side of services, including tourism, isn’t offering much support either, shrinking at an even faster rate than in July.

The anticipated recovery in the second half of the year is failing to take shape. There were good reasons to be hopeful — lower inflation and higher wages seemed like the perfect recipe for increased consumption. Plus, global industry had started to bounce back, something Germany typically benefits from. But it appears that uncertainty around economic policy has put a damper on consumer spending, while the global manufacturing upswing turned sour before German companies could feel the boost. Instead, the odds of a second straight quarter of negative growth have gone up, meaning we might be back to talking about a recession in Germany soon.

After such a prolonged slump that began in mid-2022, the renewed optimism among manufacturers seen earlier this year is fading fast. Manufacturers’ expectations towards future output have now been below the long-term average for two consecutive months, mirroring the continuous decline in outstanding orders, which have been shrinking for an uninterrupted 27 months. The anticipated interest rate cuts by the ECB, expected by most analysts, might lift spirits a little, but it’s clear that the overall mood remains poor.

11:23 AM BST

German economic gloom deepens as France gets Olympics boost

Germany’s economic woes deepened this month, while France enjoyed its fastest growth in two years as visitors flocked to Paris for the Olympic Games.

S&P Global’s composite PMI came in at 48.5 for Germany in August, below economists’ expectations and the second month of contraction.

It is the latest sign that the recovery in Europe’s largest economy has dried up after GDP unexpectedly fell 0.1pc in the second quarter.

Industry remains the main drag on Germany’s economy, with the PMI stuck in contraction since July 2022.

By contrast, the French PMI surged to 55 in August from 50.1 in July - well above forecasts. Still, the Olympics boost may not last long, with a broader slowdown predicted across Europe towards the end of the year.

11:12 AM BST

New Starbucks boss under fire for 1,000-mile private jet commute

The incoming boss of Starbucks has been plunged into an online storm over the company’s offer for him to commute around 1,000 miles by private jet.

Social media users have lambasted Brian Niccol, who has been told he does not need to relocate to the company’s Seattle headquarters from his family home in California when he takes up the role of chief executive next month.

Starbucks has instead offered the incoming boss a “small remote office in Newport Beach” which will be “maintained at the expense of the company”, but said he must commute to the headquarters when required.

The offer letter adds that the 50-year-old will be eligible to use a corporate aircraft for “business related travel”, for “travel between city of residence and the company’s headquarters”, and for “your personal travel” in accordance with company policies, up to $250,000 £191,500) per year.

Critics were quick to point out the discrepancy between this jet-setting and Starbucks’ sustainability efforts elsewhere, such as banning plastic straws.

Alcohol-free Gen Z drive surge in soft drink sales Alcohol soft drinks Gen Z

Demand for soft drinks is surging as young people cut back or even give up on alcohol altogether, data shows.

My colleague Daniel Woolfson has the details:

Almost a third of people aged 18-24 are drinking less, with 13pc completely abstaining from alcoholic drinks, according to CGA data.

This has led to an 8pc jump in sales of soft drinks in the nation’s pubs and bars, and a 2.7pc jump in hotels, as young people seek out healthier lifestyles - although CGA said sales in the total soft drinks market were flat.

It comes amid a rise in so-called ‘zebra striping’, where young people alternate between alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks on nights out so as to avoid getting too intoxicated or causing hangovers.

Diageo, the maker of Guinness, last month credited Gen Z with doubling the sales of non-alcoholic Guinness, which now accounts for 3pc of all global Guinness sales.

However, night club and hospitality bosses have warned that successive generations of students are not going out and partying like they used to, casting doubt on the sustainability of many businesses that previously relied on them for trade.

As well as a growing inclination towards health and moderation, the high cost-of-living has also been blamed for higher levels of abstention, with bosses arguing inflation has disproportionately affected the young.

Shoppers warned over ‘murky and confusing’ loyalty card discounts

Shoppers have been warned about “murky and confusing” loyalty discounts after researchers found some deals may not be as good as they appear.

Consumer group Which analysed the pricing history of more than 12,000 products at health and beauty retailers and supermarkets to discover how genuine the discounts were.

The research found “dubious discounts” and some items that were always on offer, suggesting they do not always provide the value for money shoppers might expect.

Which also found examples where prices were raised for a brief period before going on “offer”, while in some cases non-member prices were raised on the same day the loyalty promotion began.

The consumer group said the finding showed why guidance on how consumer laws apply to pricing promotions needs to be updated to clarify how it applies to loyalty pricing.

Ele Clark, Which retail editor, said:

Loyalty cards are increasingly big business, with the explosion in two-tier pricing meaning shoppers will often pay a lot more if they aren’t a member of the retailer’s scheme. But while the discounts can look impressive, many shoppers are growing suspicious of non-member prices that seem high.

We looked at the pricing history of thousands of products and found that, while the majority of discounts were not misleading, there were some questionable non-member prices and some examples that looked like an outright rip-off. Meanwhile some products were always, or almost always, on loyalty promotion, making it difficult to spot a genuine deal.

Guidance on pricing laws needs to be updated to include loyalty pricing, to help  regulators crack down if businesses break the rules. The CMA should continue to monitor loyalty pricing practices across key consumer sectors and be ready to use its new powers to take action against retailers that don’t comply.
